clue.text: Old-style dress not all will be trying

parts.note: tire is an archaic word for attire or clothing
some means a part rather than the whole

explanation.surface: Someone tries on old-fashioned clothes, though not everyone is willing to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be' is only a link joining the wordplay to the definition 'trying'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trying is tedious and wearing, a synonym pair.

clue.text: It's the country for Christmas!

parts.note: reads as a holiday destination, but names both a nation straddling Europe and Asia and the bird roasted for the festive dinner

explanation.surface: A travel slogan recommending a nation for the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive roast bird shares its name with the Anatolian republic.

clue.text: What 9 does about the team

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A question about how a numbered player behaves around the rest of the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' points to the answer to 9 across, an occupant; what an occupant does is live somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant dwells in a place, which is the verb meaning to live there.

clue.text: The chairman's battle?

parts.note: a chairman here is one who carries an enclosed chair on poles, whose chair bears the name of a French town where an 1870 battle was fought

explanation.surface: A company head's boardroom fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The carried chair type and the Franco-Prussian battle share the name of a town in the Ardennes.

clue.text: Writing about irritation caused by beastly food containers

indicators.note: the letters for writing are placed around the word for irritation

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
anger is strong irritation

explanation.surface: Something written in annoyance about troughs for livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused by' is a link; 'beastly' just means for beasts, not nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Troughs from which cattle and horses eat are the familiar stable feeders.

clue.text: A craftsman who made an ass of himself

definitions.text: A craftsman who made an ass of himself

parts.words: A craftsman who made an ass of himself
parts.note: the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream is literally given a donkey's head

explanation.surface: A workman who behaved foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream is transformed by Puck into a donkey-headed figure.

clue.text: Management slip-up

explanation.surface: An administrative blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means supervision and also a mistake made by failing to notice something.

clue.text: Not all of the litter was attributable to the church

definitions.text: Not all of the litter was attributable to the church

parts.words: Not all of the litter was attributable to the church
parts.note: under the old tenth-part levy, one piglet in ten of a sow's brood was owed to the parish clergy

explanation.surface: Rubbish around the place could not all be blamed on the churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a tenth of farm produce, including one young pig from each brood, was paid to the clergy.

clue.text: Exercising charms on top people

indicators.note: putting the letters to work, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone uses their personal magnetism on senior figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings and queens are people at the very top of society.

clue.text: The occupant tries working without a study

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other
the letters are set to work, hence rearranged

parts.note: a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: Someone living here keeps trying to work despite having no study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking: the anagram (from 'working') wraps the study.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who lives in a place is its inhabitant.

clue.text: Not up-to date, being retrogressive, but made progress

indicators.note: going backwards, so the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
new means modern or up to date

explanation.surface: Someone old-fashioned and backward-looking nevertheless advanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being retrogressive' reverses NOTNEW to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on means to continue or advance, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: There's little land in oasis left uncultivated

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some small patch of desert oasis remains unfarmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncultivated' only completes the picture of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island is a little piece of land in water.

clue.text: Compromises-offers greens and mash

indicators.note: to mash is to crush up, so these letters are pulped into a new order

explanation.surface: A menu offering vegetables and mashed potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offers' is a link; 'mash' is the anagram signal rather than potato.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise something is to put it at risk, a synonym.

clue.text: She has a right cut

explanation.surface: A woman who is entitled to a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip wool or hair off is to cut it.

clue.text: Rings about back-up work

indicators.note: the two ring letters are placed around the other piece

parts.note: O is a ring shape; two rings give two O-like letters, here OS read as O's

indicators.note: the word up is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rings are placed around support work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' is plural, so two ring-shaped letters; 'back-up' splits into the reversal signal and its fodder, and 'about' makes the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical or literary piece is an artist's numbered creation.

clue.text: Even before a dispute he seeks legal redress

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: plain means level or even
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Even before the row, this person is going to court.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a lawsuit is the complainant in court.

clue.text: Shingle may be used in this country

indicators.note: the letters may be turned into something else, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: Pebble beaches can be found in this nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The national tongue of England is the one spoken here.

clue.text: Strippers-they save their money

definitions.meaning: tools for taking off paint or wallpaper
people who scrimp and save, scrape together cash

explanation.surface: Exotic dancers who are thrifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint-removing blades and penny-pinchers both take the word from the verb to scrape.

clue.text: The person bringing in intimate letters for Her Majesty

parts.note: to import is to signify or hint, as to intimate
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone delivering private letters to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters for' is a link, signalling that ER is a pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who brings goods into the country from abroad.

clue.text: Scope for the firm with a thousand to spend

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to pass time is to spend it

explanation.surface: The range available to a business with a thousand pounds of budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or extent is a synonym, as in the reach of a subject.

clue.text: A position calling for sound sense

indicators.note: the word for sense is said aloud, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A stance that demands good common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling for' is a link, and 'sound' signals the homophone rather than meaning sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or spot where something is placed.

clue.text: Smart and trim egghead

parts.note: to trim is to cut
the head, or first letter, of egg

explanation.surface: A clever intellectual with a neat haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd or clever is a sense of the word, as in a sharp move.

clue.text: A chopper's cold, the French allege

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
le is French for the
to aver is to assert or allege

explanation.surface: The French claim that a helicopter is chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'chopper' stands for 'is', a link; 'chopper' suggests a helicopter but is a butcher's knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy butcher's knife for hacking meat.

clue.text: Casual garment for the weekend the one and only one

parts.note: the end letter of week
I is the Roman numeral for one
mono means single

explanation.surface: A relaxed outfit for the weekend, the only one you need.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose Japanese wrap robe worn informally.

clue.text: Gulp maybe about a note making serious complaint

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed around the single letter
suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A gulp perhaps around a note signals a nasty illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns GULP into PLGU, 'about' puts it round A, then E follows; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly epidemic disease is a grave affliction.

clue.text: Deck where a body of sailors can hold a party

indicators.note: the first pieces enclose the party word

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A ship's deck where the navy can throw a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Step taken by an economist that means drudgery

parts.note: a tread is a step
John Stuart Mill was a British economist and philosopher

explanation.surface: A measure taken by an economist that results in tedium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by an' and 'that means' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotonous routine work, from the prison wheel walked endlessly.

clue.text: Dig some digging up, and that's material

indicators.note: brought up from below, so the word is turned backwards in a down entry

parts.note: mined means dug some ore

explanation.surface: Some excavation yields fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digging up' reverses the piece, since a down entry is read upwards; 'and that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-wearing cotton twill fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Bring on late in error

indicators.note: a mistake, so the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Bringing on a substitute late by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about or necessitate is to involve as a consequence.

clue.text: Carol's after regular service

indicators.note: the song piece follows the regular piece

parts.note: even means regular or uniform
a carol is a song

explanation.surface: Carol is chasing a regular service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican service of evening prayer.

clue.text: A good man prevailing in controversy

parts.note: ST stands for saint, a good man
rife means widespread or prevailing

explanation.surface: A good man winning through in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Conflict or bitter disagreement.

clue.text: Plain words about lip such a bloomer!

indicators.note: the plain words surround the lip word

parts.note: prose is ordinary, plain writing
a rim is a lip or edge

explanation.surface: Blunt words about cheek: what a blunder!
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow spring flower is a bloom.
